storySpine.startingBelief: I should choose the degree my friend chose to stay together.
storySpine.studentSituation: Two friends looking at a sample business task.
storySpine.observation: They both struggle with different parts of the same task.
storySpine.whyQuestionFollows: Recognizing a specific point of struggle is more useful than copying a degree choice.
storySpine.changedAction: They write down individual questions about the task rather than comparing degrees.
storySpine.visibleConsequence: They feel relief knowing it's okay to have different questions.
storySpine.channelExperience: A supportive conversation demonstrating that academic help-seeking is personal.

selected.title: The Peer Check-in
selected.audienceGap: Assuming degree choice is a social package deal.
selected.hlni: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
selected.viewerChange: Validates asking individual questions about academic tasks.
selected.concept: Recording individual sticking points in a shared task.
selected.support: The observation belongs to this activity and participant; it supports a next question rather than a general prediction.
methodSteps: Try or inspect a clearly illustrative task.
Record one point where you needed help and one question you want to investigate.
Turn the observation into a question for a real course brief or course team.
selected.interpretationRule: Use the recorded observation to choose the next question, not to select a degree from one activity.
selected.visibleProof: A person records a specific sticking point and asks a different, more useful question afterward.
selected.payoff: Students feel confident asking about their own specific confusion.
selected.limitations: A brief exercise does not measure aptitude, learning style, long-term interest or academic performance.

demonstration.input: A shared sample case study about a small business.
demonstration.visibleInput: Example: Task: Calculate break-even point for the bakery.
demonstration.observation: Student A notes they struggle with fixed costs; Student B asks about variable components.
demonstration.nextQuestion: Where can I find a breakdown of these cost components?

comparedWith.hlni: Business Organization & Management is listed in Semester I of the published JOY University B.Com Accounting & Finance and BBA Entrepreneurship Management documents whose covers say students admitted from 2025–26 onwards.
A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
The same total can result from different component values; an aggregate alone cannot tell you the underlying mix.

conceptSelection.contrast: Pre-story comparison selected different grounded insights and mechanisms: Trust = verified_curriculum_example / Curriculum-Verification; Connection = task_question_journal / Task-Journal; Discovery = aggregate_counterexample / Aggregate-Counterexample. Each has an illustrative input, observable result and next question. This is not editorial approval.

hlni.insight: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume choosing a degree is a social package deal based on friends' choices.
hlni.viewerChange: Validates asking individual questions about specific academic tasks over following peer choices.
hlni.support: The observation is a direct result of the task, allowing for a tailored investigation rather than a generalized degree selection.
hlni.payoff: The student identifies a specific gap in their knowledge and forms a concrete, useful question.

reelTitle: B.Com vs BBA: Finding Your Focus
creativeAngle: Moving from choosing a degree based on friends to choosing based on individual questions.
objective: Help students identify their personal learning needs through a practical task rather than social pressure.
targetAudience: +2 students seeking accessible, supportive guidance, including students worried about marks, confidence, or belonging

shots.name: Friendship Comparison
shots.visual: Two students sitting at a desk, looking at two different brochures.
shots.dialogue: Choosing a degree just to match your friends?
shots.cameraPerformance: Close-up on concerned faces, warm lighting.

shots.name: The Confusion
shots.visual: Student points at the brochures, looking overwhelmed.
shots.dialogue: That misses what you actually need to learn.
shots.cameraPerformance: Camera pans slightly to show the frustration.

shots.name: The Task Reveal
shots.visual: Student pulls out a sample task paper.
shots.dialogue: Try this task to find your sticking points.
shots.cameraPerformance: Action shot of paper being placed on the desk.

shots.name: The Method in Action
shots.visual: Close up of the paper reading: Example: Task: Calculate break-even point for the bakery.
shots.dialogue: Where do you struggle: fixed or variable costs?
shots.onscreenText: Example: Task: Calculate break-even point for the bakery.

shots.name: The Better Question
shots.visual: Student writes down a specific question on a notepad.
shots.dialogue: Now ask: Where can I find a breakdown of these cost components?
shots.onscreenText: Where can I find a breakdown of these cost components?
shots.cameraPerformance: Focus on the hand writing clearly.

shots.name: Final Action
shots.visual: Student smiles, feeling confident, and puts the notepad aside.
shots.dialogue: Use this to explore your own questions.
shots.cameraPerformance: Wide shot showing both students appearing more relaxed.

productionNotes.sound: Ambient room noise, no background music.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Shifting the decision process from degree comparison to personal learning inquiry.
